sanskrit: idaṃ tan mitrāvaruṇā havir vāṃ yenāgre devā amṛtatvam āyan | tenāsmai kṣatram adhi dhārayaujo 'sapatnāḥ pradiśaḥ santv asmai ||
english: O Mitra and Varuṇa, this oblation is yours, by which the gods formerly attained immortality. By that same [offering] may sovereignty and vital force be established upon him; may the directions be free of rivals for him.

sanskrit: ghṛtasya dhārā mitrāvaruṇā duhāṃ vāṃ dhenur anapasphurantī | devaḥ savitota vāyur agnir bhūtasya patir iha śarma yacchāt ||
english: O Mitra and Varuṇa, may a cow that does not kick yield you a stream of ghee. May the divine Savitṛ, and Vāyu, and Agni — the lord of all beings — grant shelter here.

sanskrit: śaṃ nas tan mitrāvaruṇā gṛṇītaṃ tṛḍhā amitrā bahudhā vi śerām | jayatu senopa ghoṣa etu pṛthak satvāno bahudhā bharantām ||
english: O Mitra and Varuṇa, sing that which is auspicious to us. May the enemies lie slain in many ways on every side. May the army be victorious; let the battle-cry go forth separately; may the warriors carry [spoils] in many ways.

sanskrit: hanāma mitrāvaruṇāv amitrān bhavāma bhadre sukṛtasya loke | pārayān naḥ savitā devo agnir jayāmedaṃ haviṣā kaśyapasya ||
english: We shall smite the enemies with [the aid of] Mitra and Varuṇa; we shall abide in the auspicious world of the righteous. May the divine Savitṛ and Agni carry us across; may this [rite] be victorious through the oblation of Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: vāto yaṃ mitrāvaruṇā tad āha viśvantaraṃ nirmitaṃ kaśyapasya | adhvaryavo maruto yasyāsan tena devebhyo varimāṇi cakruḥ ||
english: Vāyu declared to Mitra and Varuṇa what Kaśyapa's universal oblation is fashioned for. The Maruts, who were its adhvaryus, made wide spaces for the gods thereby.

sanskrit: acikradat svapā iha bhavad agne yajasva rodasī urūcī | āmuṃ naya namasā rātahavyo yuñjantu suprajasaṃ pañca janāḥ ||
english: O Agni, the beautiful-worker cried out; be here! Sacrifice to the wide-embracing heaven and earth. O you whose oblation is given — lead him hither with reverence; may the Five Peoples yoke [him who is] endowed with good offspring.

sanskrit: dūre cit santam aruṣāsa indram ā cyāvayantu sakhyāya vipram | yad gāyatrīṃ bṛhatīm arkam asmai sautrāmaṇyādadhṛṣan ?tu devāḥ ||
english: May the ruddy [steeds] stir Indra — even when far away — to come for friendship, the wise one. When the gods consecrated for him the Gāyatrī, the Bṛhatī, and the hymn through the Sautrāmaṇī [sacrifice], they dared it.

sanskrit: adbhyas tvā rājā varuṇo juhāva somas tvāyaṃ hvayatu parvatebhyaḥ | indras tvāyaṃ hvayatu viḍbhya ābhyaḥ śyeno bhūtvā viśa ā patemāḥ ||
english: King Varuṇa has called you from the waters; Soma here calls you from the mountains. Indra here calls you from these clans. Having become an eagle (śyena), let us fly to settle among the clans.

sanskrit: śyenaṃ havir nayatv ā parasmād anyakṣetre aparuddhaṃ carantam | aśvinā panthāṃ kṛṇutāṃ sugaṃ te garbhaṃ sajātā abhi saṃ viśadhvam ||
english: Let the oblation bring the eagle hither from the far [realm], roaming unobstructed in another domain. May the Aśvins make the path easy for you; O kinsmen, enter together the embryo [of sovereignty].

sanskrit: śyenaṃ haviḥ kaśyapasyopa śikṣa- -indraṃ vātaḥ prahito dūta ā vaha | viṣahya śatrūn senāgrair viśo vṛṇāno 'va gaccha kāmī ||
english: Attend to the eagle's oblation of Kaśyapa! O wind, sent forth as messenger, bring Indra hither! Having overpowered the enemies, choosing the clans with the foremost of armies, go down [to settle], O desirous one.

sanskrit: yas te havaṃ paritiṣṭhāt sajāta uta niṣṭiyaḥ | apāca indra tān nītvā- -athemam ava gamaya ||
english: Whoever among your kinsmen or outsiders stands in the way of your call — O Indra, having led those away to the remote [quarter], then bring this one safely to rest.

sanskrit: hvayantu tvā pañca janāḥ patiṃ mitrā avṛṣata | indrāgnī viśve devā viśi kṣemam adīdharan ||
english: May the Five Peoples call you; allies have chosen [you as] lord. Indra, Agni, and all the gods have established security among the clans.

sanskrit: prajāpatir anavartiḥ sa prajābhir anavartiḥ | sa mānavartir anavartiṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: Prajāpati is one who does not turn back; he is one who does not turn back together with his progeny. May he, not turning back, make me one who does not turn back.
Indra is one who does not turn back; he is one who does not turn back together with his heroic might. [May he, not turning back, make me one who does not turn back.]

sanskrit: somo 'navartiḥ sa oṣadhībhir anavartiḥ | sa mānavartir anavartiṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: Soma is one who does not turn back; he is one who does not turn back together with the plants. May he, not turning back, make me one who does not turn back.

sanskrit: āpo 'navartayas tāḥ parjanyenānavartayaḥ | tā mānavartayo 'navartiṃ kṛṇvantu ||
english: The waters are those that do not turn back; they do not turn back together with Parjanya. May those [waters], not turning back, make me one who does not turn back.

sanskrit: devā anavartayas te 'mṛtenānavartayaḥ | te mānavartayo 'navartiṃ kṛṇvantu ||
english: The gods are those who do not turn back; they do not turn back together with immortality. May those [gods], not turning back, make me one who does not turn back.
